Already handled

It knows LTL’s quirks

The things a first LTL Freight integration learns the hard way, written into the add-on so yours doesn’t have to.

01

Freight class is a string

“77.5” and “92.50” pass; “77” is refused. No class and no default? The shipment is refused, naming the handling unit. Nothing is guessed.

02

Residential only when you say so

Taken from the residential accessorials — never from the address flag, which defaults to true at checkout and costs a fee on LTL.

03

A BOL without a PRO is uncertain

A bill of lading accepted before a PRO is assigned is not a refusal. It waits for a person instead of a second BOL being bought.

Honest about it

Built from the published API

Written against each carrier’s published documentation, without a live account. Anything that could not be confirmed is marked UNVERIFIED in the carrier class, where whoever debugs it will look.

Check before going live

  • SAIA’s REST rating and tracking response shapes
  • The NMFTA eBOL party objects’ exact nesting
  • TForce’s liftgate and limited-access codes
  • Pickups for Estes, XPO and R+L — not implemented, because the request bodies are undocumented
Test every connection in each carrier’s test environment — R+L has none, and XPO only tests bills of lading.

Needs Carrier, the gateway — $149, then $129 a year. It owns checkout pricing, the claim that stops a label being bought twice, printing, tracking and the point picker. Every add-on is free, and one licence drives all of them.

$ composer require justinholtweb/craft-carrier justinholtweb/craft-carrier-freight
$ php craft plugin/install carrier && php craft plugin/install carrier-freight
